No focal aggressive osseous lesion Summary Ms. Smith is a 70-year-old woman with a history of rheumatoid arthritis and Hodgkin lymphoma in remission. She presents with a clinical syndrome of longstanding urinary and fecal dysfunction as well as chronic UTIs, initially related to a cystocele and rectocele, but that has persisted despite correction of these defect and now has progressed to urinary retention that requires intermittent catheterizations. Additionally, there is postural instability with a couple of falls and significant imbalance, as well as a bilateral resting tremor. There is also some history of RBD, no anosmia and chronic constipation. Physical examination reveals bilateral left predominant parkinsonism without clear evidence of ataxia, gait exam shows en bloc turning and decreased arm swing, as well as decreased stride length. She is currently taking levodopa four times a day but has not noticed a dramatic improvement in her symptoms. Assessment Probable Multiple System Atrophy versus a differential diagnosis of parkinsonism including idiopathic Parkinson disease with autonomic symptoms. Urinary dysfunction may be partly attributed to prior gynecologic disease and multiple urinary tract infections however her parkinsonism is accompanied by early imbalance and postural abnormalities as well as an unclear response to dopaminergic medication, which are more suggestive of MSA. Plan - Brain MRI and MIBG scan to determine evidence of radiologic signs supportive of an MSA diagnosis as described in current consensus criteria for MSA. - Will enroll in our longitudinal cohort at BWH where we will perform serial biometric and biomarker evaluations as well as skin SAA (seeded amplification assay) for differential patterns of synuclein aggregation. Note that the latter is a research assay and the patient was informed we could not return results. Nevertheless, the results could inform triage for research and clinical protocols. Greater than 50% of the consultation involved education and counseling on these issues. The consultation duration was 60 minutes. No focal aggressive osseous lesion Summary Ms. Smith is a 70-year-old woman with a history of rheumatoid arthritis and Hodgkin lymphoma in remission. She presents with a clinical syndrome of longstanding urinary and fecal dysfunction as well as chronic UTIs, initially related to a cystocele and rectocele, but that has persisted despite correction of these defect and now has progressed to urinary retention that requires intermittent catheterizations. Additionally, there is postural instability with a couple of falls and significant imbalance, as well as a bilateral resting tremor. There is also some history of RBD, no anosmia and chronic constipation. Physical examination reveals bilateral left predominant parkinsonism without clear evidence of ataxia, gait exam shows en bloc turning and decreased arm swing, as well as decreased stride length. She is currently taking levodopa four times a day but has not noticed a dramatic improvement in her symptoms. Assessment Probable Multiple System Atrophy versus a differential diagnosis of parkinsonism including idiopathic Parkinson disease with autonomic symptoms. Urinary dysfunction may be partly attributed to prior gynecologic disease and multiple urinary tract infections however her parkinsonism is accompanied by early imbalance and postural abnormalities as well as an unclear response to dopaminergic medication, which are more suggestive of MSA.
